WGST 112.description: A social science perspective of women in psychological, sociological, historical, anthropological, economic, and political contexts; the changing roles, images, and institutions.
WGST 112.subject: WGST
WGST 112.title: Introduction to Women's and Gender Studies

WGST 113.description: Basic functioning of the female body; effects of society on processes of health and disease. Not for natural sciences credit.
WGST 113.subject: WGST
WGST 113.title: Women's Health

WGST 207.description: Anthropological study of gender, with emphasis on cross-cultural investigation of the interaction of biological, cultural, and environmental factors including intersections of race, social class, and sexuality as influences gender behavior.
WGST 207.subject: WGST
WGST 207.title: Gender and Culture

WGST 210.description: Childhood, maturity, old age, and gender socialization within the family.
WGST 210.subject: WGST
WGST 210.title: Human Life Cycles in Different Cultures

WGST 298.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of courses by title. May be repeated as content varies by title.
WGST 298.subject: WGST
WGST 298.title: Issues in Women's and Gender Studies

WGST 299.description: Supervised experience addressing a community organization’s needs and allowing the student to explore an aspect of the community related to women’s and gender studies issues. Contract approval by advisor required.
WGST 299.subject: WGST
WGST 299.title: Women's and Gender Studies Internship for Non-Majors

WGST 300.description: Offers a sociological lens to develop critical ways of thinking about sex and gender as social processes in everyday lives. This course considers how sex and gender shape and affect the experiences of women, men, girls, boys, and individuals who live in the spaces in-between (those who are intersex or transgender) across a wide range of social institutions (family, work, education, politics, etc.).
WGST 300.subject: WGST
WGST 300.title: Sex and Gender

WGST 301.description: The psychological, physiological, and social characteristics of marriage.
WGST 301.subject: WGST
WGST 301.title: Psychology of Marriage

WGST 304.description: Historical and contemporary power relationships in race, social class, gender, and sexual orientation.
WGST 304.subject: WGST
WGST 304.title: Race, Class, Gender, and Sexuality

WGST 305.description: Sociological perspectives related to various aspects of family behaviors, roles, and values.
WGST 305.subject: WGST
WGST 305.title: Sociology of Families

WGST 306.description: This course introduces anti-oppressive theoretical and applied approaches to understand and address intersections of gender and racial inequality. Social welfare policies and services available to women in contexts such as criminal justice, behavioral health, child welfare, and the military are examined.
WGST 306.subject: WGST
WGST 306.title: Gender, Race and Social Justice

WGST 307.description: Historical development of feminist theory and contemporary debates within feminism.
WGST 307.subject: WGST
WGST 307.title: Feminist Theory

WGST 308.description: An interdisciplinary survey of the contributions of African-American women to feminist theory.
WGST 308.subject: WGST
WGST 308.title: African-American Feminist Theory

WGST 309.description: Overview of theories, history, literature, politics, legal, health, and social issues connected to sexualities, including the intersections of gender, race, and social class.
WGST 309.subject: WGST
WGST 309.title: LGBTQ+ Studies

WGST 310.description: Women’s experiences: childhood and adolescence, work, family, cultural images, adjustment, and social change.
WGST 310.subject: WGST
WGST 310.title: Psychology of Women

WGST 311.description: The study of the relationship among persons of color, women, and the mass media in the United States.
WGST 311.subject: WGST
WGST 311.title: Race, Gender, and Class in Mass Media

WGST 315.description: An examination of how gendered divisions of labor shape individual and collective experiences and notions of value within socio–political and economic systems.
WGST 315.subject: WGST
WGST 315.title: Gender and Labor

WGST 317.description: An exploration of how gender shapes contemporary family life, focusing on roles, relationships, expectations, and inequalities in paid and unpaid labor across diverse families and contexts.
WGST 317.subject: WGST
WGST 317.title: Gender in Contemporary Families

WGST 320.description: Gender roles, standards of sexual behavior, evidence for women’s lives, as manifested in ancient Greek literary and archaeological evidence; attitudes toward homosexuality; the modern media’s representation of famous Greeks.
WGST 320.subject: WGST
WGST 320.title: Sexuality and Gender in Ancient Greece

WGST 321.description: Sexuality as a social construct exemplified in standards of sexual behavior in ancient Rome and their reinforcement of the ruling ideology; feminine virtue, definitions of manliness, attitudes toward homosexuality.
WGST 321.subject: WGST
WGST 321.title: Sexuality, Gender, and Power in Ancient Rome

WGST 333.description: Gender and sexuality in the shaping of social and individual identity in religious contexts.
WGST 333.subject: WGST
WGST 333.title: Sex, Gender, and Religion

WGST 334.description: Introduces feminist philosophy and applications to philosophical problems.
WGST 334.subject: WGST
WGST 334.title: Feminist Philosophy

WGST 335.description: Introduces the connection between gender and the Chinese national imagination. Readings include cultural and historical documents that purport to explain the experience of women in China. Readings in English. Taught in English.
WGST 335.subject: WGST
WGST 335.title: Women in China

WGST 336.description: Introduction to writings by and about women writers from the Arab world from the 20th and 21st centuries. Taught in English.
WGST 336.subject: WGST
WGST 336.title: Arab Women Writers

WGST 351.description: Kinship, systems of descent, marriage, and domestic organization in different cultures. Variations in childrearing practices, gender, and other aspects of social relations in kin groups.
WGST 351.subject: WGST
WGST 351.title: The Family in Cross-Cultural Perspective

WGST 352.description: Impact of gender on the distribution of power in society; foundations for intersections of gender, race, social class, and sexuality and their economic, social, and political concomitants.
WGST 352.subject: WGST
WGST 352.title: Gender and Politics

WGST 360.description: The role of women and gender in the construction of western science from historical, philosophical and sociological perspectives.
WGST 360.subject: WGST
WGST 360.title: Women and Science

WGST 379.description: Survey of women in European history from the eighteenth to the twenty-first century. Focus on women’s citizenship beginning with Enlightenment idea of rights through developments in modern feminism.
WGST 379.subject: WGST
WGST 379.title: Women in Modern Europe

WGST 381.description: Examines the dialectic between globalization and the social construction of gender. Topics include the global assembly line, transnational markets for domestic labor and sex workers, and global feminist alliances.
WGST 381.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ANTH 102 or WGST 112.
WGST 381.subject: WGST
WGST 381.title: Gender and Globalization

WGST 388.description: Anthropological study of pregnancy and birth with a cross-cultural focus comparing the United States to other nations. Examination of cultural factors such as prenatal care, dietary practices, taboos, birth location, practitioners, and birthing styles.
WGST 388.subject: WGST
WGST 388.title: Cultures, Pregnancy, and Birth

WGST 392.description: This course examines health concerns important in the lives of women around the world through an overview of contemporary issues and challenges in the field of global health, broadly construed.
WGST 392.subject: WGST
WGST 392.title: Global Women's Health

WGST 398.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of courses by title. May be repeated as content varies by title.
WGST 398.subject: WGST
WGST 398.title: Special Topics in Women's and Gender Studies

WGST 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and director of women’s studies required for undergraduate students.
WGST 399.subject: WGST
WGST 399.title: Independent Study

WGST 425.description: Interdisciplinary overview of research methods used in feminist research.
WGST 425.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in one of the following: WGST 112, WGST 304, WGST 307, or WGST 308.
WGST 425.subject: WGST
WGST 425.title: Feminist Research Methods

WGST 430.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of courses by title.
WGST 430.subject: WGST
WGST 430.title: Topics in Women's Studies

WGST 431.description: Selected small action-research project on selected issue(s) in women’s studies.
WGST 431.subject: WGST
WGST 431.title: Women's Studies Workshop

WGST 432.description: This course provides an overview of psychological, social, physical, and emotional issues related to men’s lives. Major topics include: gender construction, men and work, men and health, men in relationships, male sexualities, men in families, and masculinities in the media and popular culture.
WGST 432.subject: WGST
WGST 432.title: Men and Masculinities

WGST 433.description: A historical and global exploration of gender and sexuality in India and beyond.
WGST 433.subject: WGST
WGST 433.title: Women Love Power: Gender in Asia

WGST 437.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in both ENGL 101 and ENGL 102.
WGST 437.subject: WGST
WGST 437.title: Women Writers

WGST 445.description: This course will examine LGBTQ+ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, queer, and other nonnormative sexual identities) literatures and cultures.
WGST 445.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENGL 101 and ENGL 102.
WGST 445.subject: WGST
WGST 445.title: LGTBQ+ Literature

WGST 450.description: Exploration of LGBTQ history and communities in America from the Colonial Era to the present, using lenses of gender and sexuality to understand historical events.
WGST 450.subject: WGST
WGST 450.title: LGBTQ History in the United States

WGST 454.description: Constitutional and statutory case law dealing with gender equality issues. Topics include abortion, affirmative action, pornography, sexual harassment, fetal protection policies, employment discrimination, and women in the military.
WGST 454.subject: WGST
WGST 454.title: Women and the Law

WGST 464.description: The social, political, and economic roles and changing status of women in America.
WGST 464.subject: WGST
WGST 464.title: History of American Women

WGST 485.description: Study of rhetoric by and about women as manifested in speeches, essays, and other rhetorical artifacts.
WGST 485.subject: WGST
WGST 485.title: Women’s Rhetoric

WGST 487.description: An examination of literature by and about black women, including fiction, poetry, drama, and autobiography. This study will focus on issues that emerge from the creative representations of black women and the intersections of race, gender, sexuality, and class that interrogate what is both particular and universal experiences.
WGST 487.subject: WGST
WGST 487.title: Black Women Writers

WGST 499.description: Supervised experience addressing a community organization's needs and allowing the student to explore an aspect of the community related to women's and gender studies issues. Contract approval by advisor required.
WGST 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in WGST 112 or WGST 113; C or better in one additional WGST course at the 200-level or higher.
WGST 499.subject: WGST
WGST 499.title: Community Service Internship

WGST 515.description: Representations of race and gender in comics with a special emphasis on the experiences of African Americans.
WGST 515.subject: WGST
WGST 515.title: Race, Gender, and Graphic Novels

WGST 535.description: An exploration of the connections between oppression of women and oppression of nature.
WGST 535.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 3 hours in philosophy beyond the 100 level.
WGST 535.subject: WGST
WGST 535.title: Ecofeminism

WGST 541.description: An exploration of women’s health and health care concerns from multiple perspectives.
WGST 541.subject: WGST
WGST 541.title: Issues in Women's Health

WGST 551.description: Application of skills and theories of adolescent mentoring taught in the classroom to a supervised, structured mentoring field experience.
WGST 551.subject: WGST
WGST 551.title: Adolescent Mentoring

WGST 554.description: Impact of gender-based relations on crime and the criminal justice system.
WGST 554.subject: WGST
WGST 554.title: Women, Gender, and Crime

WGST 555.description: Approaches to gender and language emphasizing the social grounding of both; how language reflects sociocultural values and is a tool for constructing different types of social organization.
WGST 555.subject: WGST
WGST 555.title: Language and Gender

WGST 598.description: Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of courses by title. May be repeated as content varies by title.
WGST 598.subject: WGST
WGST 598.title: Special Topics in Women's Gender Studies

WGST 621.description: Public health issues, social and behavioral science, policies, programs, and services related to maternal and child health in the United States and other countries.
WGST 621.subject: WGST
WGST 621.title: Maternal and Child Health

WGST 627.description: Health status and concerns of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities. Includes an examination of measurement issues and methodological considerations in research, as well as intervention efforts targeting LGBT populations.
WGST 627.subject: WGST
WGST 627.title: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender (LGBT) Health

WGST 701.description: Examination of feminist theories and epistemologies from diverse disciplines and intellectual movements, providing an overview of historical developments in feminist discourse. Emphasis on debates surrounding such concepts as gender, identity, difference, power, and embodiment.
WGST 701.subject: WGST
WGST 701.title: Feminist Theories and Epistemologies

WGST 704.description: How contemporary feminist theory has responded to and reformulated traditional theories about the role and nature of women.
WGST 704.subject: WGST
WGST 704.title: Political Theory and Feminism

WGST 705.description: Historical and contemporary dimensions of social inequality centered in race, social class, gender, and sexuality.
WGST 705.subject: WGST
WGST 705.title: Race, Class, Gender, and Sexuality

WGST 706.description: The origins of global capitalism, the nature of money and debt, the roles of gender, race and class in social formations, and the relationship between production and reproduction.
WGST 706.subject: WGST
WGST 706.title: Engendering Global Capitalism

WGST 708.description: Impact of gender in American politics; elections, representation, rights, social movements, legal institutions, and public policy. Explores class, race, and sexuality issues within gender.
WGST 708.subject: WGST
WGST 708.title: Women in American Politics

WGST 709.description: Examines in geographical and historical contexts the activities of various women travelers and explorers.
WGST 709.subject: WGST
WGST 709.title: Women Explorers and Travelers

WGST 714.description: An examination of the particular nutritional needs of women through the life cycle with emphasis on disease prevention and how nutrition is related to a woman’s health and wellness.
WGST 714.subject: WGST
WGST 714.title: Nutrition in Women's Health

WGST 716.description: Selected topics in women’s studies that are grounded in community concerns with an emphasis on individual action-research. May be repeated for a total of 2 hours credit.
WGST 716.subject: WGST
WGST 716.title: Women's Studies Workshop

WGST 736.description: Intersections of women’s work and women’s health in diverse social, cultural, economic, geographic, and political contexts.
WGST 736.subject: WGST
WGST 736.title: Women, Work and Health: Global Perspectives

WGST 737.description: Selected topics related to works by British women authors from various periods, regions, or genres. May be repeated for credit as topics vary.
WGST 737.subject: WGST
WGST 737.title: Topics in British Women Writers

WGST 738.description: Selected topics related to works by American women authors from various periods, regions, or genres. May be repeated for credit as topics vary.
WGST 738.subject: WGST
WGST 738.title: Topics in American Women Writers

WGST 750.description: Women’s diversity explored through research on personality, stereotypes, status and power, biological aspects, socialization, sexuality, relationships, mothering, work and achievement, violence against women, psychological disorders, and feminist therapies.
WGST 750.subject: WGST
WGST 750.title: Psychology of Women

WGST 757.description: This course will acquaint students with some of the secondary literature in African American women’s history from the late nineteenth century through the twentieth century. The course examines the impact of race, gender, and class on the lives of black women and explores the historical relationship between African American women, work, family, community, and politics.
WGST 757.subject: WGST
WGST 757.title: African American Women in Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries

WGST 764.description: Selected research topics on the cultural, social, economic, and political roles and contributions of American women.
WGST 764.subject: WGST
WGST 764.title: History of American Women

WGST 767.description: Examines the application of feminist theories, concepts, and principles to social work practice. Assesses women’s experiences in society and the impact of social, political, and economic structures. Investigates feminist interventions pertaining to individuals, families, organizations, communities, and the larger social environment.
WGST 767.subject: WGST
WGST 767.title: Feminist Perspective in Social Work Practice

WGST 772.description: Different cultures’ ideas about gender and use of gender to organize social groups in a wide range of societies, including American subcultures.
WGST 772.subject: WGST
WGST 772.title: Gender and Culture

WGST 787.description: Population perspectives and demographic approaches to the measurement of gender, sexuality, and health.
WGST 787.subject: WGST
WGST 787.title: Population Perspectives of Gender, Sexuality and Health

WGST 790.description: Directed research and reading in subjects to be individually assigned.
WGST 790.subject: WGST
WGST 790.title: Directed Reading and Research

WGST 796.description: A special topic focusing on an area within women’s studies not usually covered in other graduate courses in women’s studies.
WGST 796.subject: WGST
WGST 796.title: Special Topics in Women's Studies

WGST 797.description: A capstone seminar applying women’s studies theories and methodologies to professional or discipline-based research projects.
WGST 797.subject: WGST
WGST 797.title: Seminar in Women's Studies
